methods.label: Complete the shaded part to a triangle
methods.explanation:
The five unit squares have total area \(5\), so the shaded part must have area \(\frac52\). Completing this part to a triangle avoids calculating the pieces in individual squares.

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_12B_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

Add the missing unit square with vertices \((2,0)\), \((3,0)\), \((3,1)\), and \((2,1)\) to the shaded part. The resulting region is the right triangle with vertices \((a,0)\), \((3,0)\), and \((3,3)\). Thus its area is
\[
\frac52+1=\frac72.
\]
Its vertical height is \(3\), so the triangle area formula gives its horizontal base as
\[
\frac{2\cdot\frac72}{3}=\frac73.
\]
This base also has length \(3-a\). Therefore
\[
a=3-\frac73=\boxed{\frac23}.
\]
The result lies between \(0\) and \(1\), consistent with the intersection shown. The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
